title: Hold the Line
style: folk resistance anthem, driving acoustic guitar strum, foot-stomp percussion, warm bass, restrained electric guitar swells, communal gang harmonies, earnest lead vocal, dynamic verse-to-chorus lift, raw room energy, memorable singalong hook, grounded roots-rock production
lyrics:
[Intro]
Stand up, look around
The ground is still beneath us

[Verse 1]
They sort our neighbors into sides
With polished words and sharpened pride
A headline lights a borrowed fuse
Then tells us which ones we should lose
They sell a fear, they name a foe
They count the points we have to show
But every door they build between
Was made to keep us from the scene

[Chorus]
Freedom for the stubborn and the kind
Unity for every open mind
Drop the tests, refuse the lies
Stand together, shoulder high
They can shout from every screen
We are more than what they mean
Freedom, freedom, hold the line
Your hand in mine, your voice with mine

[Verse 2]
They dress a slogan up as care
Then measure virtue in the air
A careless phrase becomes a crime
A public penance buys some time
The suits make promises in rows
While hungry towns are used for shows
And every faction claims the truth
While selling anger back to youth

[Chorus]
Freedom for the stubborn and the kind
Unity for every open mind
Drop the tests, refuse the lies
Stand together, shoulder high
They can shout from every screen
We are more than what they mean
Freedom, freedom, hold the line
Your hand in mine, your voice with mine

[Breakdown]
Ask one more question
Before you choose a side
Meet the person they condemned
And listen past the pride
Share the work, protect the weak
Let disagreement breathe
No oath, no badge, no perfect tongue
Can own what we believe

[Chorus]
Freedom for the stubborn and the kind
Unity for every open mind
Drop the tests, refuse the lies
Stand together, shoulder high
They can shout from every screen
We are more than what they mean
Freedom, freedom, hold the line
Your hand in mine, your voice with mine

[Outro]
No more borrowed battles
No more kneeling to the noise
We keep our names and common ground
We keep our human voice
